stem.en: Kabir asks why the nervous system "bothers with gaps, if the wave could just run along one very long cable". What does a gap buy?

text.en: Choice. At a synapse the next neuron adds up many inputs, some pushing it toward threshold and some away, and fires only if the sum is enough. A synapse is where a signal can be strengthened, weakened, blocked or combined. One long cable could only pass a wave on.

feedback.en: They cost half a millisecond each. They buy computation.

text.en: Gaps stop the wave getting too big.

feedback.en: Waves are all-or-none; they never get too big. Gaps are about what to do with them.

text.en: Cells cannot be longer than a metre.

feedback.en: A single neuron can run from your spine to your toe. Length is not the reason for synapses.

explanation.en: A wire carries. A synapse decides. Every place in the nervous system where inputs are weighed is a synapse.
